params.textField: The endocrine system is a system of glands that secrete hormones directly into the circulatory system. Hormones can be described as *communicators*. The word hormone is defined as a biochemical that is (normally) transported by the circulatory system to another organ to regulate physiological and behavioural activities. Many hormones are secreted in a *diurnal pattern* meaning that they show daily rhythms of secretion. When assessing levels of these types of hormones, one would need to take the blood sample at a specific time and also take note of what the person’s sleep patterns because the pattern of sleep often predicts the pattern of hormone release. Other hormones are secreted in a *cyclic variation*. For instance, the hormones of the menstrual cycle. Still other hormones like insulin and thyroid hormone are released in a pulsatile variation. Some hormones are secreted by two of the above patterns, for instance, Growth hormone is secreted in a pulsatile pattern, diurnally. Hormones have many different actions. Some *stimulate mitosis* meaning that they signal for cells to duplicate. Others like growth hormone, *stimulate protein synthesis*. Still others stimulate the release of other hormones. For instance the hypothalamus releases a number of hormones that simplistically speaking, tell the posterior pituitary to secrete hormones.

answers.text: The hypothalamus secretes Growth hormone releasing hormone (GHRH) which goes by the hypothalamus pituitary portal venous system, acting on the pituitary to release Growth hormone (GH). GH is released into circulation and rising levels of GH act in a negative feedback on the hypothalamus to decrease the release of GHRH.
An example of positive feedback occurs around day 12 of the menstrual cycle, where rising levels of oestrogen act on the hypothalamus to increase gonadotropin releasing hormone (GRH)
